title: Iron Storm
description: Non-stop kettlebell AMRAP. Bell goes down when you do.
sarge_intro: This is forty-five minutes, no half-measures, no quarter asked. You will count rounds. Bell goes down when you do.
kai_intro: AMRAP means as many rounds as possible, big dog. Not as many as is comfortable.
marcus_intro: Forty-five minutes of continuous work. Each round is a meditation. The mind quits long before the body.

title: The Centurion
description: 100 swings, 100 goblet squats, 100 rows. In any order. Against the clock.
sarge_intro: One hundred, one hundred, one hundred. That is the work. Not the goal — the minimum.
kai_intro: Three hundred reps. Move how you want, rest when you have to. Time doesn't care.
marcus_intro: The centurion runs do not ask if the road is long. They run. Three hundred reps. Begin.

title: Death by EMOM
description: Every minute on the minute for 45 minutes. Reps climb by 1 each round until you can't.
sarge_intro: Round one: one swing, one burpee. Round two: two of each. You will find your wall. The question is where it is.
kai_intro: Simple enough to explain. Hard enough to end you. Go until the minute runs out before you finish.
marcus_intro: Ascending load. Each minute the work compounds. This is a lesson in limits.

title: The Double
description: Double kettlebell complex — Front Squat, Press, Row, Swing. 10 rounds.
sarge_intro: Two bells. Ten rounds. Form does not break. If it breaks, the set ends and you start that round over.
kai_intro: Double bells means double honesty. Both sides work or neither does.
marcus_intro: The two bells teach symmetry. Weakness on one side is a debt the other side carries.

title: Snatch Test
description: 100 snatches in 5 minutes. StrongFirst standard. Scale weight as needed.
sarge_intro: The snatch test is the measure. Five minutes, one hundred reps. That is the standard. Today we find where you stand.
kai_intro: A hundred snatches in five minutes is the entry exam for serious training. You're taking it today.
marcus_intro: The snatch test does not care about your intentions. Only your preparation.

title: The Forge
description: Six movements. Six rounds. One bell. Maximum load. This is the program's hardest session.
sarge_intro: Six rounds. Six movements. No substitutions. This is the session the program was built toward.
kai_intro: The Forge. Six rounds means six chances to hold it together. Most people fall apart around round four.
marcus_intro: The Forge does not produce strength. It reveals what was already there. Six rounds. Begin.

title: Run the Gauntlet
description: Run 1 mile. 50 swings. Run 1 mile. 40 clean and press. Run 1 mile.
sarge_intro: Run. Swing. Run. Press. Run. That is all. Three miles and ninety reps. Clock is running.
kai_intro: The gauntlet. You come out the other side or you don't. Three miles and ninety reps.
marcus_intro: The gauntlet has no middle option. You enter, you finish.
